good: The grass is rooted at every tide and width I tried. The full Beaufort harness passes all 24 cases at 390, 320 and 430 (exit 0). On this-morning I swept 0, .03, .06, .1, .15 through .45, .5 through .93 and .95/.97 at 320, 375, 390, 430 and 760, and every foot is on land or mud. The only feet in water are on a spring high.

The check is real. I added only the measuring tags (data-ground, data-grass and the BFT_GRASS_WET constant, nothing drawn) to origin/main's index.html and ran the branch's harness on it. It fails this-morning at Josh's 375 width: 7 of 36 feet at .15, 13 at dead low, 3 at mid tide, and the right corner foot (238.0, 190.6) over open water at .8. At 430 it fails 10 and 19 of 40. Every one of main's 24 cases fails at 390. So it would have caught this morning's live page.

The drawing is consistent beyond what the check asks for. With the check temporarily changed to a continuous requirement from mean tide up to .94, the branch still passed at all five widths (I reverted that edit).

Porters Neck and Shady Spring are untouched. Across 24 loads (mb and sp, at 320, 390 and 430, on noon, Josh's 8:35 morning, a rainy afternoon, Halloween night and a January snow), the scene markup on every layer matches main character for character once animation delays are set aside. All the code changes are inside lowcountryScene, plus two constants and the pure bftGrassMud.

It reads right on the phone. Along each bank's river side there is a dark wet mud band, inked like the flats with a wet shine at the waterline, so the spartina stands on a bank and not against the river. The corner shoulder is a believable cut bank running down into the flat. The flats keep their look and tide behaviour. The spring high is the approved picture, with the river up around the stems. It looks right at night, at golden hour, in fog, rain and the storm, and on Halloween night.

The motion rules hold. Everything new is on the still #sceneSvg. The tufts keep their draws (the new seeds 7741, 7753 and 6611 are separate mulberry streams) and stay on #sceneFx. Under reduced motion the page has 0 animations. No filter, no new animation, and the wrack colour goes through air() and so tone().

The tests pass in both zones: `node --test test.mjs` is 73 of 73 under TZ=America/New_York and under TZ=UTC. No old assertion was weakened, and the CACHE assertion moved to v101 in the same commit as sw.js. The this-morning case matches the brief field for field and sits at the end of CASES under the required comment. AGENTS.md's paragraph sits with "The tide is drawn."
fixes: Merge order, before shipping: feature/bft-fishing-water already sets sw.js CACHE to mbwx-shell-v101 and also edits tools/beaufort/scene.mjs and test.mjs, and feature/bft-oak-glow will bump CACHE too. Whichever branch lands second must take v102 (the third v103) and update test.mjs's `/mbwx-shell-v101/` assertion in the same commit. Then re-run `node --test test.mjs` and the grass cases on the merged page, because the oak branch edits the #sceneSvg template next to the new `${grassFoot}${wrackSvg}` line.

Make grassCheck's requirement continuous. In tools/beaufort/scene.mjs, `need = t <= .5 ? 1.5 + (.5 - t) * 2 : 0` drops from 1.5 units at .50 to nothing at .501. So a regression between mean tide and .94, with feet seen against the river at .6, would pass, and cases at a nominal .5 land either side of the jump (on main, fog, storm and windy at 0.50 passed while the sweep's exact .5 failed 3). Ramp it to 0 at BFT_GRASS_WET instead, for example `t < BFT_GRASS_WET ? 1.5 * (BFT_GRASS_WET - t) / (BFT_GRASS_WET - .5) : 0` above .5. I ran exactly that on the branch at 320, 375, 390, 430 and 760 for tides .5 to .93 and everything stayed rooted. Update the test.mjs regex that pins the GRASS_TIDES line if needed.

Make the bank's line one source of truth. BANKS in lowcountryScene restates landL's and landR's control points by hand (`[-12,bankY-1.4],[W*.1,bankY-3.6]...`). Build landL and landR from BANKS[i].top, or both from one array, so a later change to the land's outline cannot leave the mud band on the old line. The harness catches only some kinds of drift.

Leave off-frame feet out of the check, for example skip x < 0 or x > W in grassCheck. On main the failures included `(-6.0, 189.8) seen against air`, a foot in the -6 to 0 overhang that no phone shows. A failure should name only grass someone can see.

Optional, ask Josh: at dead low the left bank's dark band is about 12 CSS px at 390. I think it reads as an exposed muddy bank, but if he finds the stripe heavy, BFT_GRASS_MUD at 3.5 and lighter lcfoot stops are the knobs. Below about 3 the check's mean-tide margin trips, by design.
